newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS WHIP PANTHERS TO EARN SUPER BOWL TRIP.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS WHIP PANTHERS TO EARN SUPER BOWL TRIP.

text.p: Brett Favre caught fire after a slow start to lead the Green Bay Packers back to the Super Bowl promised land with a 30-13 victory over the second-year Carolina Panthers in the NFC championship game on Sunday.

Favre, Green Bay's star quarterback and the league's Most Valuable Player the past two seasons, passed for two touchdowns and running back Dorsey Levens emerged as an unlikely hero with 205 yards of total offence.

The Packers, winners of the first two Super Bowls in 1966 and 1967 under legendary coach Vince Lombardi, will make their first trip back to the National Football League championship in 29 years on January 26 in New Orleans.
"Hey Green Bay, how about this, guess where we're going," Packers general manager Ron Wolf shouted to the crowd at the post-game trophy presentation.
In Super Bowl XXXI the Packers will face the winner of the AFC championship game between the New Engand Patriots and the upstart Jacksonville Jaguars.

Green Bay extended its home winning streak to 18 games. But the contest was the first title game at frigid Lambeau Field since the famed 1967 "Ice Bowl" that put the Packers into their last Super Bowl and the victory set off a joyous celebration among the Green Bay faithful in the packed stands.
Carolina reached the NFC championship by knocking out the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday, becoming the first expansion team to defeat a defending Super Bowl champion in the playoffs.
An interception and a fumble by Favre in the first half allowed the Panthers to establish early leads of 7-0 and 10-7.
"They like to test me and today was no different," said Packers coach Mike Holmgren. "But the players deserved this trophy, they earned it and we're not finished yet."

Favre settled down after his two miscues and played a near perfect game the rest of the way. He completed 19-of-29 passes for 292 yards and Levens caught five passes for 117 yards and rushed for 88 yards on just 10 carries.
Edgar Bennett gained 99 yards on 25 carries, while the Green Bay defence stifled Carolina's running game, limiting the Panthers to 45 yards on 14 carries.
The turning point came late in the first half as the Packers scored 10 points in the final 48 seconds of the second quarter.

Favre's six-yard scoring pass to Antonio Freeman with 48 seconds to go in the half gave Green Bay its first lead at 14-10. The touchdown capped a masterful 15-play, 71-yard drive that consumed nearly eight minutes.
The key play in the drive was a 22-yard pass from Favre to Andre Rison on 2nd-and-25 to the Carolina 6-yard line.
On the first play after the kickoff, Tyrone Williams made a diving interception of a pass by Carolina's Kerry Collins at the Green Bay 38 with 35 seconds left in the half.
Favre then marched the Packers 48 yards in 25 seconds before a 31-yard Chris Jacke field goal gave Green Bay its 17-10 lead at the intermission.
The Packers opened the second half with an 11-play, 73-yard scoring drive that lasted 6:44 and resulted in a 32-yard field goal by Jacke to increase their lead to 20-10.
The Panthers responded with an 11-play, 73-yard drive that ended with a 23-yard field goal by John Kasay that pulled them within 20-13, but the Packers shut down Carolina the rest of the way.
Meanwhile, Green Bay moved 74 yards in just three plays as Levens, who had caught Favre's first touchdown in the second quarter, turned a screen pass into a 66-yard gain to the Carolina 4-yard line.
Bennett scored on a four-yard run on the next play with 1:58 to go in the third to give Green Bay a 27-13 advantage.

The Packers capitalised on a Carolina turnover 35 seconds later when defensive tackle Gilbert Brown stripped the ball from running back Anthony Johnson and Leroy Butler recovered the fumble at the Panthers 47.
The Packers drove to the 11 and settled for Jacke's 28-yard field goal with just over 10 minutes left in the fourth quarter to complete the scoring.
"This is what we play our whole lives for," said Favre.
"Getting to the Super Bowl was our goal for the last three years. Finally."
